cosy-lesson.title: "I knew that with a mouth like mine, I just hadda be a star or something.": Barbra Streisand

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Self-image – the way a person sees, values, and interprets their own appearance and character.

p.em: Example: Refusing to get plastic surgery helped her maintain a highly healthy and proud self-image.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unconventional – different from what is normal, expected, or standard in a social context.

p.em: Example: Her voice and nose were unconventional by Hollywood standards, which made her a unique icon.

cosy-blockquote.p: To stand out – to be noticeably different or much better than ordinary people or things.

p.em: Example: Instead of trying to fit in, she chose to use her distinctive features to stand out in crowds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Upbringing – the way a child is raised, educated, and socialized by their family.

p.em: Example: Her difficult upbringing taught her to rely entirely on her own determination and talent.

cosy-blockquote.p: Perception – the way people understand, see, or interpret a person or a cultural idea.

p.em: Example: The general public perception of beauty was highly rigid when she first entered the entertainment industry.

cosy-blockquote.p: Confidence – a strong belief in one's own abilities, appearance, or personal value.

p.em: Example: Her performance on stage was full of confidence, silencing all of her critics instantly.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stereotype – a fixed, oversimplified, and often unfair idea about how a certain group should look or act.

p.em: Example: She constantly challenged the boring stereotype of how a female star ought to behave.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity – the unique combination of traits, values, and features that define who a person is.

p.em: Example: Her nose was not a weakness, but a key component of her proud personal identity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ambition – a strong, continuous desire or goal to achieve something great through hard work.

p.em: Example: Her quiet ambition was backed by an extraordinary work ethic and vocal talent.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insecurity – uncertainty, anxiety, or lack of confidence about oneself or one's appearance.

p.em: Example: Every star has some level of insecurity, but she refused to let it guide her choices.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does refusing to conform to standard beauty expectations protect a person's self-image?
★ Have you ever felt your own self-image was threatened by social media filters or trends?

Why are unconventional traits often highly attractive and memorable in a famous star?
★ What is an unconventional feature of your own style or voice that you love today?

How can a person use their distinctive features to to stand out in a highly competitive job market?
★ Do you prefer to blend into a crowd, or do you like to stand out in social groups?

How does a supportive upbringing build the confidence required to challenge major stereotypes?
★ What is the most important lesson from your upbringing that shaped your confidence?

Why is the general public perception of beauty often extremely narrow and boring?
★ How has your personal perception of successful living shifted over the last five years?

At what point does healthy confidence cross the line into arrogance or pride?
★ When was the last time you had to pretend to have absolute confidence when you felt nervous?

How does a rigid stereotype about appearance harm young artists trying to enter the industry?
★ Have you ever felt limited or pre-judged by a social stereotype?

Why is a strong, stable identity essential for anyone wanting to build a lasting career?
★ What aspects of your personal identity are you most unwilling to compromise on?

How does having a massive, quiet ambition help people overcome moments of deep insecurity?
★ How did you manage to overcome your greatest personal insecurity as a teenager?

Why do we often confuse a person's lack of arrogance with a state of personal insecurity?
★ If you had to describe your childhood relationship with parental ambition in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: Which path is most fulfilling for a creative person in the long term? Rank them: - 🌟 Mainstream Stardom Achieving massive global fame, meeting standard expectations, but sacrificing a part of your personal identity. - 🎨 Niche Artistry Remaining completely unconventional, enjoying a small loyal following, and staying 100% genuine. - 🏢 The Backstage Genius Using your visionary skills behind the scenes to guide others, avoiding the public spotlight and pressure. - 🛠️ The Independent Builder Creating your own small business or brand entirely on your own terms, accepting heavy initial responsibility.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will allow us to completely design our own physical appearance, making natural self-image obsolete. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if standard beauty perception models were completely managed by AI filters?

Future societies will completely ban plastic surgery, celebrating only highly unconventional and natural faces. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use smart technology to artificially boost your stage confidence?

In the coming decades, the desire to to stand out will be seen as a negative sign of narcissistic behavior. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where individual identity is fully standardized by social scores?

As automated technology advances, families will use virtual reality environments to manage a child's upbringing. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you protect kids from peer stereotype pressure?

In the future, social status will be determined by how much confidence a person has rather than their material wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope personal ambition will play in your own professional future over the next decade?

A future world governed fully by logic will leave no space left for the quiet mystery of individual identity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to exercise greater personal choice to fight your insecurity?

Future generations will look back at today's entertainment industry stereotype standards with deep shock. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about the danger of insecurity to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make it incredibly difficult to maintain a truly unique style. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic city that guarantees complete safety at the cost of your freedom?

One day, being an always convenient, conforming worker will be seen as a complete lack of ambition. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you feel you need to practice greater unconventional thinking right now?

A future world governed fully by smart logic will leave no space left for the beautiful struggle of overcoming insecurity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a futuristic app could guarantee you would never feel insecurity, would you use it?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
